projects.title: Website Modernization Migration from Jekyll to Hugo

projects.description: The preCICE website is built on Jekyll with several Ruby gems that have become difficult to maintain (many of which have been abandoned) and cause frequent build failures for contributors. The goal is to move the site to Hugo (a static site generator built on Go), which handles most of what these plugins do out of the box. This means porting layouts from Liquid to Go templates, upgrading from Bootstrap 3.3.7 to Bootstrap 5, and restructuring content to fit Hugo's model. All existing URLs and external documentation integrations will be kept intact during the transition. Deliverables include a fully functional Hugo site, rewritten CI/CD workflows, Algolia search via JSON output, and sub-repo mounts replacing Jekyll submodules. By the end, any contributor should be able to clone the repo and build the site in one command, with no Ruby setup required.

projects.description:
This project aims to improve the system testing framework of preCICE to make end-to-end simulations faster, more reliable, and easier to extend. Currently, system tests involve building multiple combinations of tutorials, adapters, and core versions using Docker, executing coupled simulations, and validating outputs against reference data.

The project will focus on optimizing test execution time through parallelization and caching strategies, improving result validation and reporting for better debugging, and enhancing the modularity of test configurations to simplify adding new scenarios. Additionally, improvements in CI integration will ensure more robust and automated testing workflows.

The expected deliverables include a redesigned and optimized system testing pipeline, improved reporting mechanisms, reduced execution time, and comprehensive documentation for contributors. These enhancements will strengthen the reliability and scalability of preCICE’s testing infrastructure.
